title: Over the Horizon
briefing: The board asks for an emerging risk review: what could matter in three to five years that nobody owns yet.
You have the external scan, client interviews and the strategy team's assumptions.

context.text: The refrigerant transition is already on the enterprise profile; the board wants to know what else is coming.

evidence.title: External scan
evidence.body: Refrigerant phase-down (2027); electric refrigerated trucks viable by about 2029; pharma clients halving supplier panels; heatwaves twice as frequent as a decade ago; data-sharing requirements in pharma contracts.

evidence.title: Client interviews
evidence.body: Three of the top five clients plan to require live temperature data feeds by 2027. Two will score suppliers on emissions.

evidence.title: Strategy assumptions
evidence.body: Diesel fleet to 2032. Heatwave days: flat. Client panels: stable.

questions.prompt: Which strategy assumptions does the evidence challenge?

options.label: Diesel fleet to 2032, against emissions scoring and EV viability by about 2029
Flat heatwave days, against a doubling over a decade
Stable client panels, against pharma clients halving supplier panels
Revenue growth of 6% a year
options.feedback: Not directly challenged by this evidence.

questions.prompt: Which emerging risk is most urgent for Valtren?

options.label: Losing panel places at pharma clients that will require live data feeds by 2027: it combines shrinking panels with a capability Valtren lacks
options.feedback: Nearest deadline and highest revenue at stake.

options.label: Heatwaves alone
options.feedback: Real and growing, but partly addressed by Coldline 2.

questions.prompt: How should Valtren respond to emerging risks generally?

options.label: Name an executive owner for each, define signposts that would trigger action, and review them twice a year
options.feedback: Ownership and signposts turn speculation into managed uncertainty.

options.label: Invest heavily now in every one
Wait until they become current risks

questions.prompt: Where do emerging risks sit in governance?

options.label: A standing emerging-risk section in the board risk report, with a deep dive once a year
options.feedback: Keeps them visible without swamping current risks.

options.label: Only in the strategy team's papers
options.feedback: Separates risk from the strategy it threatens.

questions.prompt: How do you frame this for a sceptical CEO who calls it 'crystal-ball gazing'?

options.label: Lead with the client interviews: three of the top five clients told us what they'll require by 2027
Warn that Valtren could go bust
options.feedback: Alarmism without evidence loses the room.

lesson: Emerging risks become manageable with evidence, an owner and signposts. Challenge the strategy's assumptions, not just its execution.
